recentTopics.description: Publish and compare environmental observations through shared formats and tools, so readings from different programmes can be read together instead of living in separate files. The programme maintains one observation schema that each project can emit against, a shared instrument-metadata block so comparisons stay honest about hardware, and a platform that stores and displays the results. It also defines how observations are screened and qualified before publication, and a public explorer that will let anyone browse what the programmes have published.

recentTopics.description: Develop low-cost, open stations that record river-water conditions continuously and reliably enough to be trusted outside the lab. The programme pairs a repeatable calibration procedure with firmware that buffers and recovers through interruptions, then proves the whole station on the bench before installing it at a real river site under a written deployment checklist. Everything the programme learns is meant to be reproducible by other teams from the published procedure and the shared observation format.
recentTopics.name: RiverWatch
recentTopics.summary: RiverWatch develops low-cost river-water monitoring stations, pairing an open calibration procedure with bench integration and field trials at candidate sites.

recentTopics.description: Build portable air-quality monitors that a single person can carry on foot through a neighbourhood and trust to give comparable readings. The programme selects its particle sensor by comparing candidate instruments against a reference baseline, then checks the choice over extended comparisons and changing humidity before it commits. It also validates field measurements against reference samples taken along repeated traverses of the same route, so a survey result can be explained and repeated rather than merely recorded.
